---
title: "The data"
---



Western States Survey (YouGov), fielded in 2020 and 2024 in Arizona, Colorado, Nevada,
New Mexico, and Utah. `R/00_build_data.R` reads the two raw Stata files, harmonizes
them, and writes the one analysis file distributed here. The raw files are not
distributed; the CSV is.


::: {.cell layout-align="center"}

```{.r .cell-code}
wss_raw <- read_csv("data/wss_2020_2024.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
dim(wss_raw)
#> [1] 7600   20
```
:::



::: {.cell layout-align="center"}

```{.r .cell-code}
count(wss_raw, year)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 2
#>    year     n
#>   <dbl> <int>
#> 1  2020  3600
#> 2  2024  4000
```
:::


## What is in it


::: {#tbl-vars .cell layout-align="center" tbl-cap='Columns of `data/wss_2020_2024.csv`.'}

```{.r .cell-code}
tibble(
  variable = names(wss_raw),
  type     = map_chr(wss_raw, ~ class(.x)[1]),
  n_miss   = map_int(wss_raw, ~ sum(is.na(.x))),
  distinct = map_int(wss_raw, n_distinct)
) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

The substantive columns, per the codebooks in `codebooks/`:

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `year`, `state` | survey year; AZ, CO, NV, NM, UT |
| `weight` | survey weight (see below) |
| `vote_choice` | Trump / Democrat / Other / Did not vote |
| `vote_type` | whether the vote was `reported` or `intended` |
| `trump_vote` | 1 Trump, 0 Biden/Harris, `NA` otherwise |
| `age`, `female`, `race`, `latino` | demographics |
| `educ` (1–6), `college`, `faminc` (1–16) | education and income |
| `pid7`, `ideo5` | party identification and ideology |
| `auth1`–`auth4` | child-rearing items; 1 = authoritarian response |

::: {.warn}
[The weight is already harmonized]{.warn-head}
The 2020 file calls it `weight` and the 2024 file calls it `weight_all`;
[`R/00_build_data.R`](https://github.com/crweber9874/UNM_Workshop/blob/main/R/00_build_data.R)
renames the latter, so this file has a single `weight` column. An agent told "use the
2024 weight" will go looking for `weight_all` and not find it. This is exactly the kind
of thing that belongs in `AGENTS.md`.
:::

## The outcome

`trump_vote` is defined only for two-party voters, which is where most of the missingness
lives:


::: {.cell layout-align="center"}

```{.r .cell-code}
count(wss_raw, year, vote_choice) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = year, values_from = n)
#> # A tibble: 5 × 3
#>   vote_choice  `2020` `2024`
#>   <chr>         <int>  <int>
#> 1 Democrat       1717   1936
#> 2 Did not vote     78    217
#> 3 Other           126    115
#> 4 Trump          1164   1678
#> 5 <NA>            515     54
```
:::



::: {.cell layout-align="center"}

```{.r .cell-code}
wss_raw |>
  summarise(n_obs  = sum(!is.na(trump_vote)),
            n_miss = sum(is.na(trump_vote)),
            .by = year)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 3
#>    year n_obs n_miss
#>   <dbl> <int>  <int>
#> 1  2020  2881    719
#> 2  2024  3614    386
```
:::


Reported and intended vote are not the same measurement, and the mix differs by year —
something the analysis chapter has to take seriously:


::: {.cell layout-align="center"}

```{.r .cell-code}
count(wss_raw, year, vote_type) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = year, values_from = n)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 3
#>   vote_type `2020` `2024`
#>   <chr>      <int>  <int>
#> 1 intended     636   1846
#> 2 reported    2449   2100
#> 3 <NA>         515     54
```
:::


## The authoritarianism items

Four forced-choice child-rearing pairs, each scored 1 for the authoritarian response:


::: {.cell layout-align="center"}

```{.r .cell-code}
wss_raw |>
  select(year, auth1:auth4) |>
  pivot_longer(auth1:auth4, names_to = "item") |>
  summarise(mean = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE),
            n_miss = sum(is.na(value)),
            .by = c(year, item)) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = year, values_from = c(mean, n_miss)) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

::: {.cell-output-display}


|item  | mean_2020| mean_2024| n_miss_2020| n_miss_2024|
|:-----|---------:|---------:|-----------:|-----------:|
|auth1 |     0.563|     0.541|           2|           3|
|auth2 |     0.385|     0.383|           1|           2|
|auth3 |     0.308|     0.346|           2|           0|
|auth4 |     0.519|     0.506|           1|           7|


:::
